extracted.subtask_description: MPEP guidance for examiners on claim drafting defects and proper bases for rejections/objections (indefiniteness, omitted elements/steps, new matter, duplicate claims, disclaimer, foreign filing, final rejections, reissue limits, res judicata). Used to prepare Office actions and apply statutory/regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Antecedent Basis in the Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] recites the limitation [2] in [3]. There is insufficient antecedent basis for this limitation in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the limitation which lacks antecedent basis in bracket 2 with its location. Example wording: --said lever-- or --the lever--. This form paragraph may be modified for other instances of indefiniteness and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Claims (recitation of a use without steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] provides for the use of [2], but, since the claim does not set forth any steps involved in the method/process, it is unclear what method/process applicant is intending to encompass. A claim is indefinite where it merely recites a use without any active, positive steps delimiting how this use is actually practiced. Claim [3] is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because the claimed recitation of a use, without setting forth any steps involved in the process, results in an improper definition of a process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert what is being used (e.g., 'the monoclonal antibodies of claim 4' for a method for using monoclonal antibodies to purify interferon). See Ex parte Dunki and Clinical Products v. Brenner; see MPEP §2173.05(q). This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Are a Literal Translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims are generally narrative and indefinite, failing to conform with current U.S. practice. They appear to be a literal translation into English from a foreign document and are replete with grammatical and idiomatic errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph to indicate claims are narrative/indefinite due to literal translation; must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'For Example'
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'for example' renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitation(s) following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP §2173.05(d). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'Or The Like'
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'or the like' renders the claim(s) indefinite because the claim(s) include(s) elements not actually disclosed (those encompassed by 'or the like'), thereby rendering the scope of the claim(s) unascertainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2173.05(d). Use form paragraph only after preceding form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'Such As'
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'such as' renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2173.05(d). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifier of 'Means' Lacks Function (35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the word 'means' is preceded by the word(s) '[2]' in an attempt to use a 'means' clause to recite a claim element as a means for performing a specified function. However, since no function is specified by the word(s) preceding 'means,' it is impossible to determine the equivalents of the element, as required by 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words preceding 'means' must convey a function. Example: 'latch means' is definite because 'latch' conveys the function 'latching' (i.e., 'means for latching' makes sense). 'Conduit means' is indefinite since 'conduit' has no functional connotation. In such cases use this form paragraph and precede with 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Steps Omitted (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being incomplete for omitting essential steps, such omission amounting to a gap between the steps. The omitted steps are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2 recite the steps omitted from the claims and give the rationale for considering them critical or essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Elements Omitted (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being incomplete for omitting essential elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the elements. The omitted elements are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2 recite the elements omitted from the claims and provide rationale for considering them critical or essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Cooperative Relationships Omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being incomplete for omitting essential structural cooperative relationships of elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the necessary structural connections. The omitted structural cooperative relationships are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2 recite the structural cooperative relationships omitted and give the rationale for considering those relationships critical or essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 112, 2nd Paragraph - Omnibus Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite in that it fails to point out what is included or excluded by the claim language. This claim is an omnibus type claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph to reject an 'omnibus' type claim. No further explanation necessary. This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. See MPEP §1302.04(b) for cancellation by examiner's amendment upon allowance. Example: 'A device substantially as shown and described.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark or Trade Name as a Limitation in the Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] contains the trademark/trade name [2]. Where a trademark or trade name is used in a claim as a limitation to identify or describe a particular material or product, the claim does not comply with the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A trademark identifies the source of goods, not the goods themselves; therefore the claim scope is uncertain. In bracket 2 insert trademark/trade name and where used; in bracket 3 specify the material/product identified. See Ex parte Simpson. Use appropriate form paragraph and precede as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate Claims (substantial duplicate under 37 CFR 1.75)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims in an application are duplicates, or else are so close in content that they both cover the same thing, despite a slight difference in wording, it is proper after allowing one claim to object to the other claim under 37 CFR 1.75 as being a substantial duplicate of the allowed claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.05.05 (warning) and 7.05.06 (objection) may be used. 7.05.05 advises applicant that if claim [1] is found allowable, claim [2] will be objected to as a substantial duplicate; use when duplicate claims are present but not allowable to give opportunity to correct. If duplicate claims are not allowable, use 7.05.05; if allowable, use 7.05.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Matter (35 U.S.C. 132) - No amendment shall introduce new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention. In amended cases, subject matter not disclosed in the original application is sometimes added and a claim directed thereto; such claims are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New matter includes addition of unsuppported subject matter, adding specific percentages/compounds after a broader original disclosure, or omission of a step from a method. See Waldemar Link v. Osteonics, In re Rasmusson, MPEP §§2163.05-2163.07(b) and §§608.04-608.04(c). Examiner must be alert to detect new matter; use 35 U.S.C. 132 as basis for objection to amended abstract, specification, or drawings. If new matter added to claims, use 7.31.01 rejection rather than 7.28 objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to New Matter Added to Specification (Form Paragraph 7.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed [1] is objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132 because it introduces new matter into the disclosure. The added material which is not supported by the original disclosure is as follows: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant required to cancel the new matter in reply. Not for reissue applications (use 14.22.01). In bracket 2 identify new matter by page/line numbers and/or drawing figures and explain why not described in the specification as filed, addressing any applicant statements and unresolved questions raising doubt as to possession at filing. If new matter affects claims, also make rejection under form paragraph 7.31.01; if new matter added only to a claim, do not use this paragraph but use 7.31.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Filing Without License (35 U.S.C. 182-185) - Abandonment and Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention disclosed in an application subject to an order under section 181 may be held abandoned if in violation the invention has been published or an application filed in a foreign country without the Commissioner's consent. Except when authorized by license, a person shall not file in any foreign country prior to six months after filing in the United States an application for patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 184-185 set out license requirements and that failure to procure license can bar a U.S. patent unless through error without deceptive intent. Examiner who learns of a corresponding foreign application filed before the U.S. application had been on file for 6 months and where invention was apparently made in U.S. should refer the application to Licensing and Review Section of Group 3640. Pending investigation, prosecution may continue; Licensing and Review will request transfer if action under 35 U.S.C. 185 is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer (claims disclaimed by applicant's actions/inaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be rejected on the ground that applicant has disclaimed the subject matter involved. Such disclaimer may arise, for example, from the applicant's failure to: (A) make claims suggested for interference, (B) copy a claim from a patent when suggested by the examiner, or (C) respond or appeal within the time limit to the examiner's rejection of claims copied from a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection on disclaimer applies to all claims not patentably distinct from the disclaimed subject matter as well as to the claims directly involved. Use Form Paragraphs 7.48 and 7.49 for such rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To Present Claims for Interference (Form Paragraph 7.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. [2] based upon claim [3] of Patent No. [4]. Failure to present claims and/or take necessary steps for interference purposes after notification that interfering subject matter is claimed constitutes a disclaimer of the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only after applicant has been notified that interference proceedings must be instituted and applicant has refused to copy the claims. In bracket 2 insert --102(g)-- or --102(g)/103(a)--. In bracket 4 insert patent number and 'in view of _____' if another reference is relied upon. When rejection is under 103(a), include basis for obviousness. Note that interferences may include obvious variants (see MPEP §2306).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection, Disclaimer, Failure To Appeal (Form Paragraph 7.49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] stand finally disposed of for failure to reply to or appeal from the examiner's rejection of such claim(s) presented for interference within the specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.661 and 1.663. Use when applicant fails to reply or appeal within time, resulting in final disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections Following an Interference or Public Use Proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections may be based on the outcome of interference or public use proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2363.03 for interferences and 37 CFR 1.292 and In re Kaslow for public use proceedings. Upon termination of a public use proceeding, send notice to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences to resume interference proceedings promptly if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res Judicata as a Ground for Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Res judicata may constitute a proper ground for rejection but is restricted; it should be applied only when the earlier decision was by the Board of Appeals or a reviewing court and when there is no opportunity for further court review of the earlier decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply with care. When making a res judicata rejection, also ordinarily act on the basis of prior art. The MPEP lists cases where res judicata rejections were sustained and cases where they were reversed; consider differences in claims, new evidence, and prior decisions when applying res judicata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue (35 U.S.C. 251) - enlargement of claim scope barred after 2 years
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 251 forbids granting a reissue 'enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent' unless applied for within two years from the grant of the original patent. Such a bar is absolute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims broader in any respect than original patent claims may be rejected as barred by 35 U.S.C. 251. When reissue applied for within two years, examiner does not go into the question of undue delay. A defective reissue oath is ground for rejecting all claims in the reissue application. Note reissue applications are 'special' and remain so even without prompt reply. See MPEP Chapter 1400 and applicable case law (e.g., In re Bennett).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Previously Allowed Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall thereafter be rejected only after the proposed rejection has been submitted to the primary examiner for consideration of all the facts and approval of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give full faith and credit to prior examiner's search/action unless clear error or other prior art is known. Examiner should not take an entirely new approach or make a new search merely hoping to find something. When rejecting a previously allowed claim, point out in the letter that the claim was previously allowed using Form Paragraph 7.50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Previously Allowed, Now Rejected, New Art (Form Paragraph 7.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: The indicated allowability of claim [1] is withdrawn in view of the newly discovered reference(s) [2]. Rejection(s) based on the newly cited reference(s) follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert the name(s) of the newly discovered reference(s). Any action including this form paragraph requires the signature of a Primary Examiner. See MPEP §1004.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rejection (37 CFR 1.113) - when a rejection/action may be made final
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) On the second or any subsequent examination or consideration by the examiner the rejection or other action may be made final, whereupon applicant's reply is limited to appeal or to specific amendment rules. (b) Examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable, clearly stating reasons in support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before making a final rejection develop a clear issue between examiner and applicant. Thorough search and fully applied references are expected in the first action. Do not make hasty or ill-considered final rejections. Statement of grounds in final rejection must allow applicant to judge advisability of appeal; may refer to prior complete statements if applicable. Final rejection letter should conclude with Form Paragraph 7.39. See 37 CFR 1.113 and guidance on applicant rights and extension policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Is Final (Form Paragraph 7.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL. Applicant is reminded of the extension of time policy as set forth in 37 CFR 1.136(a). A shortened statutory period for reply to this final action is set to expire THREE MONTHS from the mailing date of this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains timing: if first reply filed within TWO MONTHS and advisory action delayed, shortened period may expire on advisory action mailing date; in no event later than SIX MONTHS from mailing date. Should not be used in reissue litigation cases or reexamination proceedings where 37 CFR 1.136(a) policies differ. Use Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326. For amendments after final rejection see MPEP §§714.12-714.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rejection, When Proper on Second Action (R-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under present practice, second or any subsequent actions on the merits shall be final, except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant's amendment of the claims nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the relevant period with fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information submitted in an IDS during the permitted period with fee is used, the examiner may use it and make the next Office action final provided no other new ground (not necessitated by amendment) is introduced. A second or subsequent action in reexamination should not be made final if it includes a rejection, on newly cited art other than IDS-submitted items, of any claim not amended by applicant. Consider 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 references and possible common ownership affidavits which may disqualify references; see MPEP §706.02(l)(3). Form Paragraph 7.40 should be used where final action includes new grounds necessitated by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Is Final, Necessitated by Amendment (Form Paragraph 7.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's amendment necessitated the new ground(s) of rejection presented in this Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is reminded of extension policies under 37 CFR 1.136(a) and shortened statutory reply periods (three months, with provisions for two-month first reply considerations). Do not use in reissue litigation or reexamination proceedings where policies differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Is Final, Necessitated by IDS With Fee (Form Paragraph 7.40.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's submission of an information disclosure statement under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p) on [1] prompted the new ground(s) of rejection presented in this Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP §609(B)(2)(i). Applicant reminded of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy and shortened statutory periods. This paragraph should not be used and a final rejection is improper where there is another new ground of rejection introduced by the examiner which was not necessitated by amendment. In bracket 1 insert the filing date of the IDS containing the item used in the new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rejection, When Proper on First Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Header indicating standards for when a final rejection on the first action may be proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed standards are in the following section (not included on this page chunk). Generally, final rejection on first action is exceptional and governed by MPEP and CFR rules.
